text: Yes, I take my medications every day as prescribed. I haven't noticed any floaters or shadows in my peripheral vision, just the black spots and decreased clarity in the center of my right eye.

speaker: Doctor
text: The central location of your vision loss and black spots, combined with your HIV status, strongly suggests a retinal issue like CMV retinitis or macular edema. Since I cannot order tests, I must rely on your description: do the black spots appear to move with your eye movements, or do they stay fixed in the same spot in your visual field?

speaker: Patient
text: The black spots stay fixed in the same spot in my visual field; they don't move around when I shift my gaze. It feels like there is a permanent dark patch blocking my central vision in that eye.

speaker: Doctor
text: Fixed scotomas in an AIDS patient are highly suggestive of CMV retinitis, even without pain. Do you see any shimmering lights or "headlights in fog" appearance, and has your vision loss progressed rapidly over these two days?

speaker: Patient
text: I haven't seen any shimmering lights or a foggy appearance, just the persistent black spots. The vision loss has been pretty steady over the last two days without getting significantly worse.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the fixed central scotoma and lack of pain, I am concerned about CMV retinitis involving the macula. Do you have any history of prior eye infections or treatments, and have you noticed any floaters or flashes of light in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: No, I have never had any prior eye infections or treatments. I haven't noticed any floaters or flashes of light in the past either.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since you have no history of floaters or flashes, this makes a retinal detachment less likely. Do you notice any distortion in straight lines, such as them appearing wavy or bent, when you look at them with your right eye?

speaker: Patient
text: Yes, straight lines do appear wavy and distorted when I look at them with my right eye. It makes it difficult to read or focus on details in that eye.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of metamorphopsia confirms macular involvement, which is a critical finding in the context of your HIV status. Given the fixed scotoma, distortion, and lack of pain, I am highly suspicious of Cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis affecting the macula. DIAGNOSIS READY: CMV Retinitis
